A dedicated kernel thread (the txg sync thread)
Runs in whichever context calls it

nodes.title: Administrator
nodes.role: The person or script typing the command. Every path in this graph that a command starts begins with a wire from this node; the arrows that come back into a command node are its results, errors and refusals.

nodes.title: zpool(8) command
nodes.role: `zpool create` parses the options: `-f` force, `-n` dry run (print the layout, touch nothing), `-d` no features by default, `-o` pool properties and `feature@name=`, `-O` and `-m` root file system properties, `-R` altroot and `-t` temporary name (both default `cachefile=none`). A pool name containing `/` is refused. Hands the vdev arguments to make_root_vdev(), refuses a default mountpoint directory that exists and is not empty, builds the feature list, calls zpool_create() and on success opens, mounts and shares the root file system.

nodes.title: make_root_vdev() / construct_spec()

ref.code: make_root_vdev(zpool_handle_t *zhp, nvlist_t *props, int force, int check_rep,

nodes.role: The vdev grammar. `mirror`, `raidz[1-3]`, `draid[p][:Nd][:Nc][:Ns][:Nw]` (and `anymirror`) start a top-level vdev whose children are the following devices up to the next keyword; a bare device is a top-level vdev by itself. `special`, `dedup` and `log` mark the following top-level vdevs with an allocation bias (log accepts only disks and mirrors); `spare` and `cache` start lists that are not top-level vdevs. Each keyword checks its minimum device count. Without `:Nd`, a dRAID group gets at most 8 data disks. `-o ashift=` (9 to 16) is copied into every top-level vdev. At least one normal top-level vdev is required. Then, in order: in-use check, replication check unless `-f`, partitioning unless `-n`.

nodes.title: make_leaf_vdev()

ref.code: make_leaf_vdev(const char *arg, boolean_t is_primary, uint64_t ashift)

nodes.role: Turns one device argument into a leaf nvlist. A full path keeps the name given (so udev by-id names survive) but is resolved to decide whether it is a whole disk; a short name is looked up in the default device directories. A block device or whole disk becomes type `disk` with `whole_disk` set accordingly, a regular file type `file`; anything else is refused. Without `-o ashift`, drives known to misreport their sector size get an ashift from a built-in table.

nodes.title: Replication-level check
nodes.role: Skipped with `-f`. All normal top-level vdevs must have the same type and redundancy (raidz and dRAID may mix at equal parity; raidz and mirror at equal failure tolerance); a mirror or raidz must not mix files and devices or devices whose sizes differ by more than 16 MiB. Special and dedup vdevs need not match as long as they survive at least as many device failures as the normal vdevs. Log vdevs are not checked.

nodes.title: Device in-use checks

ref.code: check_disk(const char *path, blkid_cache cache, int force,
check_slice(const char *path, blkid_cache cache, int force, boolean_t isspare)
check_file_generic(const char *file, boolean_t force, boolean_t isspare)

nodes.role: Runs for every leaf, spare and cache device, even with `-f`. A whole disk must open with O_EXCL; its GPT partitions are each probed with libblkid. A ZFS label is checked with zpool_in_use(): a member of an active pool, or a hot spare of another pool (unless this device is also a spare here), can never be used; an exported or possibly active pool, or any other filesystem signature, is refused unless `-f`. A corrupt primary GPT is refused unless `-f`.

nodes.title: make_disks(): prepare disks
nodes.role: Skipped with `-n`. A disk leaf that is a partition only has its first 4 KiB zeroed (unless it is a spare). A whole disk (not held open exclusively as an existing spare) is relabelled: the udev partition link is removed, the zfs_prepare_disk script runs, a GPT is written, `zpool` waits for udev to recreate the `-part1` link, zeroes its first 4 KiB, and from then on the leaf's path names partition 1. Files are left alone.

nodes.title: zpool_label_disk(): GPT
nodes.role: Writes a new GPT with libefi. Partition 1 (type V_USR, name `zfs-` plus 16 random hex digits) starts at 1 MiB and runs to the end of the disk less 8 MiB, rounded down to a 2048-sector boundary; partition 9 is an 8 MiB reserved partition after it. The same byte offsets are used on 512-byte and 4K-sector disks. A partition under 64 MiB fails. The label is read back and checked after udev settles.

nodes.title: Feature set and compatibility
nodes.role: Reads the `compatibility` property: unset, empty or `off` means every feature, `legacy` none, otherwise the features present in all of the named files (from /etc/zfs/compatibility.d or /usr/share/zfs/compatibility.d). Unknown names in an /etc file are an error. `zpool_do_create()` then enables every feature the kernel module supports that the set allows, unless `-d` or `-o version` below 5000; `-o feature@x=disabled` removes one, and enabling one outside the set only warns.

nodes.title: libzfs / libzfs_core
nodes.role: zpool_create() checks the pool name and property values (`feature@` values become the number 0), validates the `-O` properties as file system properties and, for `-O encryption`, prepares the wrapping key. Packs the vdev tree, the pool properties (with the root file system properties nested inside) into a zfs_cmd_t and issues ZFS_IOC_POOL_CREATE directly, not through libzfs_core. Turns errors into messages, using the device and pool names the kernel returns for EBUSY and ENXIO.

nodes.title: zfs_ioc_pool_create()
nodes.role: Kernel entry for ZFS_IOC_POOL_CREATE. Unpacks the config and properties, rejects an unsupported `version`, separates the root file system properties, builds the encryption parameters and the ZPL creation properties (normalization, utf8only, casesensitivity, ZPL version) for the root dataset, and calls spa_create(). Afterwards sets the remaining root properties; if that fails, spa_destroy() removes the new pool again and the ioctl returns the error.

nodes.title: zfs_set_prop_nvlist()
nodes.role: After the pool exists, the `-O` and `-m` properties are set on the root dataset with source local, as `zfs set` would.

nodes.title: spa_create()
nodes.role: Builds a pool from nothing while holding the namespace lock. In order: name check and spa_t, activation, property and encryption checks (special or dedup vdevs need `feature@allocation_classes`), vdev tree parse, create (open and label), dRAID spares and their feature gates, aux devices, metaslabs; then the DSL pool, dedup and BRT tables, the pool objects and properties for txg 4, feature refcounts for dRAID and AnyRAID; then it starts the txg threads, waits for txg 4 to sync, writes the cache file and returns. The version is SPA_VERSION (5000, feature flags) unless `-o version` was given without features.

nodes.title: SPA namespace
nodes.role: The system-wide table of pools. spa_create() holds its lock from the name check to the end, so no other pool operation runs meanwhile. spa_add() creates the in-memory spa_t with the altroot and a cache file entry for /etc/zfs/zpool.cache (none when an altroot is set).

nodes.title: spa_activate()
nodes.role: Makes the spa_t usable: state ACTIVE, the six metaslab classes (normal, log, embedded_log, special, special_embedded_log, dedup), the zio taskqs and the per-txg lists.

nodes.title: spa_prop_validate()
nodes.role: Checks each pool property: `feature@` names must be known features with value 0, `version` must not be combined with features, booleans 0 or 1, `cachefile` an absolute path, empty or `none`, `multihost` needs a host id, `comment` must be printable.

nodes.title: spa_unload()
nodes.role: Any error inside spa_create() unwinds what exists so far: spa_unload() closes and frees the vdev tree (once there is one), spa_deactivate() frees classes and taskqs, spa_remove() takes the name out of the namespace. Nothing reaches the cache file. Labels already written stay on disk, but with pool txg 0 they do not describe an importable pool.

nodes.title: Pool cache file (zpool.cache)
nodes.role: After txg 4 has synced, writes the config of every pool that uses the same cache file into it (default /etc/zfs/zpool.cache), truncating and rewriting in place with O_SYNC. Nothing is written for `cachefile=none` or an altroot without a cache file. Posts a config sync sysevent and udev change events for the new devices. Failures are retried asynchronously.

nodes.title: spa_config_parse()
nodes.role: Recursive walk of the nvlist: one vdev_alloc() per nvlist, then its ZPOOL_CONFIG_CHILDREN. It follows only `children`: the `spares` and `l2cache` arrays beside them are not parsed into the tree. Holds every config lock (SCL_ALL) as writer.

nodes.title: vdev_alloc()

ref.code: vdev_alloc(spa_t *spa, vdev_t **vdp, nvlist_t *nv, vdev_t *parent, uint_t id,
vdev_alloc_common(spa_t *spa, uint_t id, uint64_t guid, vdev_ops_t *ops)

nodes.role: Creates one vdev_t: picks the ops vector by type (root, mirror, raidz, draid, disk, file, anymirror ...), runs the type's init hook, assigns a random guid (the root vdev's guid becomes the pool guid; others are unique within the pool), records path, devid, whole_disk and the requested ashift, sets the allocation bias of a top-level vdev from its nvlist and `vdev_islog` for log vdevs, and links it to its parent.

nodes.title: vdev_create()
nodes.role: Opens the whole tree and labels it. Unlike an import, a create allows no partial open: every vdev must come up HEALTHY.

nodes.title: vdev_open() / vdev_reopen()
nodes.role: Calls the type's open, which for interior vdevs opens the children first. A leaf below 64 MiB fails with EOVERFLOW. Usable size (asize) is the device size less 4 MiB in front (two labels plus the 3.5 MiB boot area) and 512 KiB at the end. On the first open of a top-level vdev, ashift is the requested value or else the logical ashift, raised toward the physical ashift (up to zfs_vdev_max_auto_ashift, at least zfs_vdev_min_auto_ashift) by vdev_ashift_optimize(); it is fixed from then on. Each leaf is probed with label-area reads (vdev_probe()) before the open succeeds.

nodes.title: vdev_label_init(): first labels

ref.code: spa_config_generate(spa_t *spa, vdev_t *vd, uint64_t txg, int getstats)

nodes.role: Walks the tree leaf by leaf, deliberately one at a time. Reads any existing label: one of an active pool, of a spare or cache device, or one written moments ago by this same create (the same disk listed twice) means EBUSY, with the device and the pool it belongs to recorded for the error message. Otherwise writes all four labels: the config of the pool and of this leaf's top-level vdev marked as pool txg 0 (not yet a real pool) with create_txg 4, a zeroed bootenv area, and an uberblock ring holding only a template with txg 0. Spares and cache devices get a short aux label instead.

nodes.title: Mirror vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. At create, opening a mirror opens each side; its size is that of the smallest side and its logical ashift the largest of the sides. All sides must open, as for every create.

nodes.title: RAIDZ / dRAID vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. raidz: init reads the parity (1 to 3); open needs at least parity + 1 children, and the size is the smallest child times the number of children, parity included. dRAID: init reads data disks, parity, distributed spares and groups and builds the permuted mapping of groups to children; open opens the data children, then the distributed spares, and sizes the vdev as the smallest child less a 32 MiB reserve, times the children that are not spares, rounded down to whole groups. Each dRAID metaslab is aligned to the group width.

nodes.title: dRAID distributed spares
nodes.role: For every distributed spare of every dRAID top-level vdev, appends a leaf nvlist of type `dspare` named `draid<parity>-<vdev id>-<spare id>` to the pool's spare list. From here on they are ordinary hot spares in the aux list, backed by space reserved on every child of their dRAID. Counts dRAID vdevs (and those with failure groups) for the feature checks.

nodes.title: spa_validate_aux()

ref.code: spa_validate_aux(spa_t *spa, nvlist_t *nvroot, uint64_t crtxg, int mode)
spa_validate_aux_devs(spa_t *spa, nvlist_t *nvroot, uint64_t crtxg, int mode,

nodes.role: Checks the `spares` and then the `l2cache` arrays: each entry must parse as a single leaf, which is made its own top-level vdev, opened and given an aux label; its new guid is written back into the nvlist and the temporary vdev_t is freed. At create any failure aborts.

nodes.title: Spare and cache lists (sav)
nodes.role: Builds the pool's auxiliary vdev lists from the nvlist: each spare and cache device becomes a standalone vdev_t (not part of the root vdev's tree), is opened, and is registered system-wide by guid so other pools see it as a spare or cache device. Cache devices join the L2ARC. The lists are marked to be written to the MOS in the first sync.

nodes.title: vdev_metaslab_set_size()
nodes.role: Chooses the metaslab size of a top-level vdev from its asize: aim for zfs_vdev_default_ms_count (200) metaslabs of at least 2^zfs_vdev_default_ms_shift (512 MiB), at least zfs_vdev_min_ms_count (16) metaslabs, at most 2^zfs_vdev_max_ms_shift (16 GiB) each until zfs_vdev_ms_count_limit (131072) would be exceeded, never below 16 MiB. Roughly: under 8 GB about 16 metaslabs, 8 to 100 GB one per 512 MiB, 100 GB to 3 TB about 200, larger ones 16 GiB each.

nodes.title: vdev_expand() / vdev_metaslab_init()
nodes.role: For each top-level vdev: sets the deflate ratio, creates its metaslab groups and asize >> ms_shift metaslab_t structures, each marked dirty for txg 4 (space maps do not exist yet), and marks the vdev's config dirty so its labels are rewritten in the first sync. On a normal or special vdev with more than zfs_embedded_slog_min_ms (64) metaslabs, the emptiest metaslab is moved to the embedded log group, reserved for ZIL blocks.

nodes.title: Metaslab classes and groups
nodes.role: Where a top-level vdev's space is offered. Its metaslab group joins the class of its allocation bias: log, special, dedup, or normal for everything else. Normal and dedup vdevs also get a group in the embedded log class, special vdevs one in the special embedded log class; log vdevs have only their log group. The pool's minimum and maximum ashift are tracked over normal-class vdevs only.

nodes.title: Space maps (metaslab_sync)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. In the first sync, vdev_sync() gives each new top-level vdev its metaslab array object in the MOS, and metaslab_sync() creates a space map object for each metaslab, stores its object number in that array and logs the allocations made in this txg.

nodes.title: dsl_pool_create(): the MOS
nodes.role: Creates the DSL pool and, under a transaction assigned to txg 4, the meta-object set: an empty objset of type META whose root block pointer the first uberblock will point at. Then the pool directory, scan state, the special directories, feature objects and the root dataset.

nodes.title: Root, $MOS, $FREE, $ORIGIN
nodes.role: Object 1 of the MOS becomes the pool directory ZAP. The root dsl_dir is created (it carries the pool's name in the namespace), then `$MOS` (accounts the MOS's own space), `$FREE` with the pool-wide free bpobj, and `$ORIGIN` with its `$ORIGIN@$ORIGIN` snapshot, the origin of every clone-less dataset.

nodes.title: Root dataset and file system
nodes.role: The dataset named like the pool: a dsl_dataset under the root dsl_dir, its objset (type ZFS), and the ZPL objects inside it: master node with the ZPL version and creation properties, system attribute tables, the unlinked set and the root directory znode. With `-O encryption` it also gets its crypto key (page `zfs-encryption-keys`).

nodes.title: Feature ZAPs and refcounts
nodes.role: Three MOS ZAPs list features for read, for write and their descriptions. Enabling a feature records it with refcount 0 (enabled, not active) and enables the features it depends on. A feature becomes active when its refcount rises: dRAID and AnyRAID at create, allocation_classes when a special or dedup vdev's ZAP is built in the first sync, others (avz_v2, log_spacemap ...) when first used. Only active features restrict which software can import the pool.

nodes.title: Pool directory objects
nodes.role: Entries spa_create() adds to the pool directory under txg 4: the pool history object (with a first "create" record of the software version), the config object that the first sync fills, the creation version, the deflate flag, and the deferred-free bpobj. Also sets up the in-memory dedup and block-cloning tables (their objects appear only when first used) and a random checksum salt.

nodes.title: Pool properties
nodes.role: Sets in-memory defaults, records the cache file choice, then applies the `-o` properties under txg 4: `feature@` entries enable features, `altroot`, `cachefile` and `readonly` are not stored, `comment` and `compatibility` go into the config, and the rest (including `ashift` and `autoexpand`) are stored in the pool properties ZAP. The `ashift` property itself does not set any vdev's ashift: zpool already copied it into each top-level vdev.

nodes.title: TXG: syncing (txg_sync_thread)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. spa_create() starts the quiesce and sync threads only after it has built txg 4 in memory, then waits in txg_wait_synced() until txg 4 is on disk.

nodes.title: spa_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Syncs txg 4, the pool's first: config object, aux lists, every dirty dataset and the MOS, then vdev_sync() for the new top-level vdevs. Creating space maps dirties the MOS again, so the passes repeat until nothing is dirty; then the labels and uberblock are written.

nodes.title: dsl_pool_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Writes the dirty datasets of txg 4 (the root dataset and `$ORIGIN`), then the MOS, and hands the MOS root block pointer to the uberblock.

nodes.title: Config object, vdev ZAPs, aux lists
nodes.role: Because the vdevs are config-dirty, the first pass creates the all-vdev ZAP and a ZAP for every leaf, top-level vdev and the root, stores each top-level vdev's allocation bias in its ZAP, generates the full pool config for txg 4 and writes it into the config object (it also becomes the in-memory config used for the cache file). With spares or cache devices, their lists are written as separate packed nvlist objects.

nodes.title: Uberblock + label update

ref.code: vdev_config_sync(spa_t *spa, vdev_t **svd, int svdcount, uint64_t txg,
uberblock_update(uberblock_t *ub, vdev_t *rvd, uint64_t txg, uint64_t mmp_delay)

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. The commit point of the new pool. Every top-level vdev is on the config-dirty list, so all of them get new labels. uberblock_update() fills in txg 4, the guid sum of the tree, the time and the MOS root block pointer; until it lands on disk the provisional labels say pool txg 0 and nothing is importable.

nodes.title: Label / uberblock writer

ref.code: vdev_label_sync_list(spa_t *spa, int l, uint64_t txg, int flags)
vdev_label_write(zio_t *zio, vdev_t *vd, int l, abd_t *buf, uint64_t offset,

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Order: flush caches, even labels L0 and L2 with the real config, flush, uberblock written into the ring of every label, flush, odd labels L1 and L3, flush. Spare and cache devices keep their aux labels.

nodes.title: zio create + execute

ref.code: zio_write_phys(zio_t *pio, vdev_t *vd, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size,

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Label writes are physical zios at fixed offsets under a root zio that the caller waits for; MOS and dataset blocks are ordinary write zios. Both pass the pipeline and the per-disk queue drawn in the I/O graph.

nodes.title: Leaf vdev driver
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Opening a leaf: a disk is opened by its configured path as a block device with ZFS as exclusive holder (retrying briefly while udev recreates links), and reports capacity, logical and physical block size, write cache, TRIM support and whether it is rotational. A file vdev opens a regular file and reports 512-byte sectors unless the vdev_file tunables say otherwise. Writes are then submitted as block I/O.

nodes.title: GPT partition table
nodes.role: The partition table at the start and end of a whole disk. After `zpool create` on Linux: partition 1 for ZFS, partition 9 reserved (8 MiB). Read by the in-use checks, written by zpool_label_disk().

nodes.title: Data disks (normal class)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. The leaves of the normal top-level vdevs (or regular files for file vdevs). After the first txg they hold the MOS, the root dataset and the space maps, and without a special vdev all of the pool's metadata.

nodes.title: Special vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. With a special vdev, the metadata of the first txg normally lands here.

nodes.title: Dedup vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Holds only labels and space maps after create; dedup tables appear when dedup is first used.

nodes.title: SLOG (log class)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. A log vdev gets labels and metaslabs but no data at create; the ZIL writes there later.

nodes.title: Cache device (L2ARC)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Carries only an aux label naming it a cache device (no pool guid, no vdev tree); the L2ARC feed fills it later.

nodes.title: Hot spare disk
nodes.role: A disk in the pool's spare list. It carries only an aux label (state spare, its guid, no pool guid), may be shared by several pools, and is attached in place of a failed disk later (page `zfs-fault-management`).

nodes.title: Labels L0-L3 + uberblock ring
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Four 256 KiB labels per leaf: L0 and L1 in the first 512 KiB, L2 and L3 in the last 512 KiB, each with the pool and top-level vdev config and a ring of uberblocks. After create: first the provisional set (pool txg 0), then the real config and the uberblock of txg 4.

paths.title: Create a pool on one whole disk
paths.summary: `zpool create tank /dev/disk/by-id/ata-X` from the command line to the mounted file system. The first txg is drawn as one wait here; path `first_txg` opens it up.
paths.ends: The disk has a GPT with ZFS in partition 1, four labels describing a one-vdev pool at txg 4, about 200 metaslabs with space maps (fewer on a small disk), and a MOS holding the pool directory, the root, `$MOS`, `$FREE` and `$ORIGIN` directories, the root dataset and the feature objects. The pool is in zpool.cache and its file system is mounted at /tank. The writes themselves follow `zfs-io-flow:txg_sync`.

paths.ends: One top-level vdev of the chosen type in the normal class, sized as its type dictates, with labels on every leaf. A dRAID pool also has its distributed spares in the spare list and the draid feature active.

paths.title: Failure inside the kernel, and rollback
paths.summary: Errors that only the kernel can see: a label that marks the device as in use (including the same disk named twice under different paths), a device too small, special or dedup vdevs without the allocation_classes feature, or a root file system property that cannot be set after the pool exists.
paths.ends: busy, small, feature: the spa_t, vdev tree and classes are freed and the name is free again; labels written before the failure say pool txg 0 and do not form an importable pool. rootprop: the pool had been fully created and is destroyed again.

options.label: Special or dedup vdev without feature@allocation_classes (ENOTSUP)
A -O property fails after the pool was created

model: Most of the checking happens in userspace before the kernel is asked. `zpool` parses the vdev grammar into an nvlist tree, refuses devices that are in use and (unless `-f`) layouts with mismatched redundancy, and on Linux gives every whole disk a new GPT label: partition 1 for ZFS from 1 MiB, an 8 MiB reserved partition 9 at the end. Only then is one ioctl, ZFS_IOC_POOL_CREATE, issued.

The kernel builds a tree of vdev_t from that nvlist: a root vdev (its guid becomes the pool guid), top-level vdevs (a disk, a file, a mirror, a raidz or a dRAID), and leaves. Each top-level vdev belongs to one allocation class: normal, special, dedup or log. Hot spares and cache devices are not in the tree; they are separate auxiliary lists.

Sizes and ashift are settled at the first open. Each leaf reports its capacity and sector sizes; a mirror is as large as its smallest side, a raidz is its smallest child times its width (parity included), a dRAID leaves out its distributed spares and a reserve. The ashift chosen for each top-level vdev is kept for its life.

Every leaf carries four 256 KiB labels, two at the front and two at the end. Create writes provisional labels (pool txg 0) first, leaf by leaf, so a disk that belongs to an active pool, or the same disk named twice, fails with EBUSY before anything else is written.

The whole initial pool (MOS, pool directory, root, `$MOS`, `$FREE` and `$ORIGIN` directories, the root dataset with its file system objects, feature ZAPs, pool properties, history) is built in memory by the ioctl thread inside txg 4 (TXG_INITIAL), before the txg sync thread even exists.

The first txg sync writes it all: the pool config object, one space map per metaslab, the MOS and root dataset blocks, then the labels with the real config and the first uberblock. Only when that txg is on disk does `spa_create()` write `zpool.cache`, the root file system properties get set and `zpool` mount the new file system.

Each top-level vdev is cut into metaslabs when it is created: about 200 by default, each 512 MiB to 16 GiB; normal and special vdevs with more than 64 metaslabs give one of them to an embedded log class.

A failure in userspace leaves no pool, but whole disks may already have been repartitioned. A failure inside `spa_create()` unwinds everything in memory; a failure to set the root properties destroys the just-created pool again.
simplifications: Label and block writes jump from `zio_create` to the leaf driver; the pipeline stages and the per-disk queue between them are drawn in the I/O graph.
The vdev tree is recursive: vdev_open() and vdev_label_init() run once per vdev, and spa_config_parse() once per nvlist. Each is drawn once.
Return wires are drawn only where a size, an ashift or an error matters; most returns to `spa_create` are implied by the next step.
Leaf opens for the normal class, special, dedup, log, spare and cache devices are separate wires into separate device nodes; they are the same call (`vdev_disk_open()`).
dRAID is folded into the RAIDZ node, as in the I/O graph; AnyRAID (`anymirror`) appears only in node text.
The first txg is shown as one sync with its main writes; the second and later passes of spa_sync(), deferred frees, the log space map and MMP are left out.
`zpool create -n` (dry run), `-t` (temporary name), boot environments and encryption key handling are described in node text only.

page.title: ZFS Pool Creation
page.intro: This spec describes a diagram of `zpool create`: how the command line becomes a vdev specification, which checks can refuse the disks, how Linux whole disks are repartitioned, how the kernel turns the specification into a vdev tree (single disk, file, mirror, raidz, dRAID, special, dedup, log, plus the spare and cache lists that stay outside the tree), how sizes, ashift and metaslabs are decided, what labels are written at once, how the meta-object set (MOS), the root dataset and the feature objects are built for the first txg, and what is on disk once that txg has synced.
